key_insight: OmniStream introduces a single streaming visual backbone that jointly handles perception, 3D reconstruction, and action in real time by using causal spatiotemporal modeling, closing the gap between image-level perception, offline temporal models, and spatial geometry systems.
problem_solved: Current vision foundation models are fragmented and either focus on static image semantics, offline temporal reasoning, or separate geometric reconstruction, making them ill-suited for continuous, real-time agent tasks that require integrated perception, memory, and decision-making.
method: Design a unified streaming backbone with causal spatiotemporal attention to process continuous visual input without future lookahead, preserving real-time causality.
Integrate modules for semantic perception, geometry-aware reconstruction, and action-conditioned outputs within one network, trained with multi-task objectives for joint capabilities.
Employ streaming-friendly memory and computation strategies (e.g., temporal compression, incremental updates) to maintain low latency and persistent world representation.
impact: OmniStream enables practical, real-time embodied agents and interactive systems by providing a single, efficient model that reasons about what is seen, reconstructs 3D structure, and produces action-ready representations—reducing system complexity and improving responsiveness.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram showing a streaming input pipeline → causal spatiotemporal attention backbone → branching heads for perception, reconstruction, and action.
Timeline visualization comparing causal streaming processing vs. offline/batched temporal models (latency vs. accuracy).
Before/after panel: fragmented multi-model stack vs. unified OmniStream stack with fewer components and lower end-to-end latency.
Radar or bar chart summarizing improvements across metrics (perception accuracy, reconstruction quality, latency, robustness).
paper_title: OmniStream: Mastering Perception, Reconstruction and Action in Continuous Streams
paper_authors: Yibin Yan, Jilan Xu, Shangzhe Di, Haoning Wu, Weidi Xie
